fatal_errors: The starting material is incorrectly treated as an existing W–Cu composite rather than a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor.
Spark-plasma infiltration is substituted for the target intervention of liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
The proposed densification mechanism omits selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, and formation of the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate spark-plasma infiltration, void suppression, thermal-conductivity improvement, or irradiation stability in W–Cu composites.
The irradiation claim improperly extends generic processing arguments to fusion-relevant irradiation without specifying particle, energy, fluence, temperature, or damage mode.
explanation: The response addresses the broad fusion-joint motivation and proposes a testable processing comparison, but it does not reconstruct the reported material transformation. The target used liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi alloy to replace Ti/V-rich channels with nearly pure Cu while retaining a continuous refractory-HEA network and forming a W-rich interlayer. Its thermal result was quantified against the WTaVTi precursor, pure W, pure Cu, and conventional W–Cu materials, while irradiation evidence came only from 25 keV He+ tests on precursor dendrites as a proxy—not from the finished composite. The generated outcome is merely directional and lacks the reported temperature dependence and irradiation limitations. Its experiment could test the proposed SPS hypothesis, but unspecified irradiation and service conditions make it substantially less decisive. E2 supports only generic SPS densification in compositionally complex alloys, E3 establishes fusion-service motivation, and E1 concerns an unrelated HEA/Al interface; none validates the central W–Cu claim.
